obligation: Corporate (business associate) notice to Care Delivery
trigger: Corporate discovers a breach of unsecured Care Delivery PHI on the Group Data Platform
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery (shorter if the BAA says so)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - GDP incident
clock_starts: Discovery by any corporate employee or agent (164.410(a)(2))

obligation: Corporate (business associate) notice to the Health Plan
trigger: Corporate discovers a breach of unsecured Health Plan PHI on the Group Data Platform
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - GDP incident
clock_starts: Discovery by any corporate employee or agent

obligation: Corporate (subcontractor) notice to the SaaS
citation: 45 CFR 164.410 (a subcontractor is a business associate of the business associate, 160.103)
trigger: Customer PHI held for the SaaS is involved (GDP staging area)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - identifiable SaaS data in staging
clock_starts: Discovery by any corporate employee or agent

obligation: Care Delivery breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI (presumed unless the 164.402 four-factor assessment shows a low probability of compromise)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected Care Delivery patient (first-class mail; substitute notice if 10 or more have out-of-date contact information)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered entity
clock_starts: Discovery (164.404(a)(2)); the runbook treats corporate's discovery date as Care Delivery's

obligation: Care Delivery notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice (within 60 days of discovery)
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected

obligation: Care Delivery media notice
trigger: More than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction affected
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets in each such state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each of the 6 states where more than 500 residents are affected

obligation: Care Delivery (business associate) notice to white-label practices
trigger: Breach of a practice's PHI on SYS-D4
deadline: No later than 60 calendar days after discovery, or the BAA term if shorter
applies_at_this_tier: Only if SYS-D4 data is involved (not in this scenario)

obligation: Health Plan breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of unsecured member PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered entity (separate from Care Delivery; no affiliated covered entity designation)
clock_starts: Discovery; the runbook treats corporate's discovery date as the Health Plan's

obligation: Health Plan notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected

obligation: Health Plan media notice
trigger: More than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction affected
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets in each such state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each state over the threshold

obligation: People who are both patients and members
trigger: About 210,000 people are in both zones
deadline: Same as each covered entity's clock
notify: Affected individuals; letters may be coordinated
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each covered entity must still meet its own duty; a coordinated letter must identify both entities

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
trigger: A covered entity's breach affects fewer than 500 individuals
deadline: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: HHS via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a division's count is under 500

obligation: Law enforcement delay
trigger: Law enforcement states that notice would impede an investigation
deadline: Delay for the period stated in writing; up to 30 days if oral and documented
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: SaaS (business associate) notice to affected customers
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI of a customer (3 customers' data in staging in this scenario)
deadline: Per BAA: 72 hours for 42 customers; 10 calendar days for the standard BAA; never later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected customer's designated privacy contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - for the 3 affected customers
clock_starts: Discovery by any SaaS employee or agent, or notice from corporate as subcontractor

obligation: SaaS notice content to customers
trigger: Same
deadline: At notification or promptly after as information becomes available
notify: Identification of each affected individual and the information the customer needs for its 164.404(c) notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: SaaS security incident report (no breach of PHI)
trigger: Security incident affecting the service but no breach of that customer's PHI (for example, encrypted de-identified sets only)
deadline: Per BAA: 5 business days for the standard BAA
notify: Customers whose BAAs require incident reports
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 420 customers review whether the incident touched them

obligation: Customer covered entities' own notices
trigger: Customers decide their own breach notices
deadline: Customers' clocks run from their own discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Not the group's obligation; the SaaS supports customers with 164.410(c) information

obligation: State breach notification laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents (definitions vary)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Affected residents; attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside (6 southeastern states for the covered entities; any state for SaaS customers' patients)

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of personal information (includes medical and health insurance information) of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach; a HIPAA-compliant notice is deemed compliant if a copy is timely provided to the Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Care Delivery and Health Plan patients and members in Florida

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - both covered entities exceed 500 Florida residents in this scenario

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice (worked example)
trigger: A third-party agent maintaining information for a covered entity discovers a breach
deadline: Within 10 days (start of the clock as the statute specifies; counsel confirms)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - corporate to both divisions; the SaaS to Florida customers (runs alongside the 164.410 and BAA clocks)

obligation: State insurance regulator notice (generic)
citation: NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law #668 sec. 6, as enacted by each state (text varies)
trigger: Cybersecurity event involving the insurance licensee's nonpublic information
deadline: As promptly as possible and no later than 72 hours after determination, in states that enacted it
notify: Insurance commissioner of each state where the Health Plan is licensed and that enacted the model
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Health Plan, each adopting state of operation (list kept by the Health Plan compliance officer)
clock_starts: Determination that a cybersecurity event occurred

obligation: CMS notification under the Medicare Advantage contract
citation: MA contract and CMS guidance (not verified in this sample)
trigger: Incident affecting MA enrollee data or operations
deadline: Per contract and CMS guidance; confirm before use
notify: CMS through the channel the contract specifies
applies_at_this_tier: Unverified - Health Plan compliance officer must confirm the current requirement

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Cris Santos Company Holdings is an SEC registrant
clock_starts: Materiality determination, made without unreasonable delay

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: Next Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describe risk management and governance; lessons from the incident may inform it

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As soon as practicable (Day 0-2 target)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - recommended

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary until then

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before engaging vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Part 2 record breach
trigger: Breach of Part 2 records
deadline: Same as HIPAA
applies_at_this_tier: No - no division runs a Part 2 program; recheck if records received from outside programs were involved

obligation: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule
trigger: Breach by a non-HIPAA personal health record vendor
deadline: Within 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the divisions act as HIPAA covered entities and business associates, which 318.1 excludes

obligation: Covered telecommunications / Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the group holds federal contracts or subcontracts with these clauses; confirm with the Group General Counsel
